chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya and Hammad, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: Do not pray the Maghrib prayer until you arrive at Jam', so pray Maghrib and the last Isha prayer there with one Adhan and two Iqamas. Descend into the valley floor on the right side of the road, near the Mash'ar. It is recommended for the first-timer to stand at the Sacred Mash'ar, tread upon it with his foot, and not pass the basins on the night of Muzdalifa.

And he should say: 'O Allah, this is Jam'. O Allah, I ask You to gather for me therein all encompassing goodness. O Allah, do not make me despair of the goodness which I ask You to gather for me in my heart. And I seek from You to make known to me what You made known to Your Guardians in this my station, and to protect me from all encompassing evil.'

And if you can stay awake during that night, then do so, for it has reached us that the doors of the sky are not closed that night for the voices of the believers, who have a humming sound like the humming of bees.
Allah, Exalted is His Praise, says: 'I am your Lord, and you are My servants. You have fulfilled My Right, and it is a Right upon Me to answer you.'
Thus, Allah removes from whom He wills their sins that night, and forgives whom He wills.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءَكَ: Your Guardians, referring to the Imams or divine favorites.
key_terms.الْمَشْعَرُ الْحَرَامُ: The Sacred Mash'ar (Monument), a key site for standing during Hajj.
key_terms.جَمْعٌ: Jam', a specific location in Muzdalifa where pilgrims combine prayers.
key_terms.جَوَامِعَ الْخَيْرِ: All-encompassing goodness, a concept in supplication asking for comprehensive divine blessings.
key_terms.دَوِيِّ النَّحْلِ: Humming of bees, a metaphor for the sound of believers' voices.
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ الْمُزْدَلِفَةِ: The night of Muzdalifa, the night spent between Mina and Muzdalifa.

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended prayers and supplications for the night of Muzdalifa in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details the specific rites of Muzdalifa, emphasizing the consolidation of Maghrib and Isha prayers with a single Adhan and two Iqamas, a practice rooted in Shia jurisprudence. It prescribes descending to the valley near the Sacred Mash'ar for supplication, highlighting the night's unique spiritual atmosphere where the 'doors of heaven' remain open to the believers' voices, facilitating divine forgiveness and the accumulation of good deeds.
